tools.name: list_overlays
tools.description: Find animated overlays by topic, family or niche. Returns compact preset choices and editor links. Reuse the same filters and pass the returned next_cursor as cursor for another page.

tools.name: get_overlay
tools.description: Inspect an overlay preset's editable fields, types, allowed values and limits, looks, aspects, duration and free status before configuring it. Each field has relevant (the preset's layout and options use it now) and showWhen (the conditions under which it is used; absent means always). cues lists the taps the overlay declares (id, kind, at in overlay seconds, when) for sound placement; most overlays declare none.

tools.name: configure_overlay
tools.description: Configure an animated overlay with editable values, look, aspect, duration or background. Returns its configuration URL, free/Pro tier, relevance (field ids the final configuration uses or does not), activeCues (taps this exact configuration has, usable as sfx overlay-cue ids; empty when it has none) and inactiveEdits (requested values kept but unused by this layout, with a notice). Field errors list allowed inputs so you can correct and retry. Changes to free preset text generally need Pro to render.

tools.name: render_overlay
tools.description: Start a local animated overlay render and return job_id. MP4 uses green screen by default; MOV is transparent ProRes 4444; WebM is transparent VP9. Needs the user's FFmpeg. Free configurations need no login; others need Pro. Poll job_status for the file.

configuration.description: The relative configuration URL returned by configure_overlay.

tools.name: add_overlay_to_video
tools.description: Render an overlay transparently and composite it onto one local video (up to 60 seconds) at start_seconds. Automatically selects and reauthorizes the nearest supported aspect, returned as aspect. The start must fit the overlay within the video. Returns job_id; poll job_status. Produces H.264/AAC MP4 with audio, source aspect, long side capped at 1920. Local media never uploads. Use edit_video for longer or multi-clip edits.

configuration.description: The relative configuration URL returned by configure_overlay.

tools.name: edit_video
tools.description: Create a local video with sequential v1 clips and nonoverlapping v2 clips above them. Every clip requires track; v2 requires start seconds, v1 forbids start. Crop uses source-edge percentages; place selects full, halves, corner picture-in-picture or a custom normalized box. Omitted crop/place mean zero crop/full. Supports trims (at least 3 frames (0.1 seconds)), fill/fit, pan (0–1), zoom (1–3), photos (0.1–30 seconds), audio and source-second punch-ins. Up to 300 clips, maximum end 180 seconds. after_clip indexes the request array and must target v1; the incoming neighbor is the next v1, skipping v2. Transitions clamp to adjacent clip limits. Captions and pause detection use v1 only, even when muted. Removing pauses ripples both tracks and overlays; conflicting v1 transitions return an explicit error. Align sources manually; no automatic sync or drift correction. Example: put reference.mp4 on top muted, me.mp4 on the bottom, crop 5% off the sides, start together, Clean captions from my voice. Captions are made on your computer in English; optional corrections replace exact words/phrases. Specify caption style clean/boxed/minimal/karaoke/bold-keyword/word-pop/highlight-box/neon/pop-up/typewriter/outline/editorial/gradient/mixed, position upper/center/lower and size s/m/l. Style mixed gives every word its own font, weight, color and spacing; add captions.mix with a preset (creator or editorial), seed and palette, and captions.word_styles to restyle chosen words by source seconds (font, weight, italic, fill, tracking, leading, underline, highlight). Example: mixed-font Creator trio captions with a cream, yellow and pink palette, underline the words spoken from 2.0 to 2.8 seconds in the first clip. Titles: texts adds up to 100 native titles of up to 120 characters, each either bound to a clip (v1 or v2) by clip (shown for that clip's whole span; optional timestamp source = the clip's source in-point as mm:ss, or timeline) or placed with start and duration timeline seconds. Defaults: sans 800, size m, centered, no backing; set font, weight, italic, fill, size, x, y and backing to restyle. Plain titles are free and never leave your computer. A title may take reveal (a rectangular wipe over stationary text) and occlusion (behind the people in one clip); the texts schema gives each field, default and rule, and either needs Pro to export. Examples: “Wipe 'Grand opening' in from the left over half a second” is texts [{text:"Grand opening", clip:0, reveal:{direction:"right", duration:0.5}}]; “Put the title 'Sunday reset' behind me in this clip from 1 to 4 seconds, near the top, with a soft edge” is texts [{text:"Sunday reset", start:1, duration:3, y:0.25, occlusion:{clip:0, feather:2}}]. Rapid intro: rapid_intro takes 5–7 v1 clip indices in teaser order and one label per clip; it prepends a 3–6-frame cut (frames_per_clip, default 5) of each clip's trim, muted by default, then plays the unchanged v1 body with each clip's label and timestamp (source in-point mm:ss by default; timeline or none). Everything with an absolute time (v2 starts, overlay starts, explicit titles) moves later by the intro length, so give those times as for the edit without the intro. Build it in one call. This tool never looks at pictures: use the descriptions the user gives or ask for them, and never invent them from file names. Example: “Make a five-frame rapid intro from grind.mp4, pour.mp4, stir.mp4, steam.mp4 and serve.mp4, then replay them with source timestamps and the labels Grind beans, Pour water, Stir, Steam milk and Serve, in 9:16.” is one call with five v1 clips, rapid_intro {clips:[0,1,2,3,4], frames_per_clip:5, timestamp:"source", labels:[{clip:0,text:"Grind beans"},…]} and aspect 9x16. No overlays or unchanged free overlays with Clean/Boxed/Minimal captions and no word_styles export without login; plain titles and rapid intro are free; titles with a reveal or behind people, mixed captions, word styles and other edits need Pro. 1080p default, 720p also free. Media never uploads; Studio exports never enter account history. Returns job_id; poll job_status. Motion: clips, texts and overlays take an optional motion object of keyframe channels x, y, scale, rotation and opacity, each [{at, value, easing}], that moves, scales, rotates or fades the whole layer over its finished picture. zoom is static inner framing; motion.scale is outer motion. at is source seconds for footage (photos: seconds on the photo's own clock, from its in) and local seconds from its own start for titles and overlays. x and y are fractions of the output width and height (positive right and down), scale is a multiplier, rotation is clockwise degrees, opacity is 0–1. easing is hold, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out or a custom [x1, y1, x2, y2] curve with each number 0–1, and shapes the segment after its key; values hold before the first and after the last key. Example: “On the first clip, smoothly zoom from 100% at source 0s to 120% at 2s, then slide 15% left by 3s; fade 'Watch this' in over its first half-second, in 9:16.” is clips[0].motion {scale:[{at:0,value:1,easing:"ease-in-out"},{at:2,value:1.2,easing:"linear"}], x:[{at:0,value:0,easing:"hold"},{at:2,value:0,easing:"ease-in-out"},{at:3,value:-0.15,easing:"linear"}]}, texts [{text:"Watch this", start:0, duration:4, motion:{opacity:[{at:0,value:0,easing:"ease-out"},{at:0.5,value:1,easing:"linear"}]}}] and aspect 9x16. Footage and title motion are free. Any non-identity motion key on an overlay, even on a free preset, needs Pro; keys that all equal the neutral value (x 0, y 0, scale 1, rotation 0, opacity 1) stay free. Sounds: sfx places up to 100 short effects from the built-in free sound pack, and nothing else (no other audio, music or links). The sounds are click: ugc-click-01 (Interface click), ugc-click-02 (Mouse click); typing: ugc-typing-01 (Keyboard burst), ugc-typing-02 (Single mechanical key); whoosh: ugc-whoosh-01 (Bamboo swish), ugc-whoosh-02 (Air sweep); pop: ugc-pop-01 (Bubble pop), ugc-pop-02 (Mouth pop); sparkle: ugc-sparkle-01 (Cartoon sparkle), ugc-sparkle-02 (Magic chime). Give each exactly one of start (timeline seconds of the edit before pause removal and any rapid intro, which move it with the edit) or anchor: title-enter {text: index in texts}, transition {after_clip: index of a v1 clip listed in transitions}, overlay-cue {overlay: index in overlays, cue: a tap id from that overlay's activeCues}. offset moves an anchored sound up to 2 seconds either way. Optional in/out (seconds inside the sound), gain, mute, fade_in, fade_out. A sound needs its title, transition or tap to exist; a missing one is an error naming the field. auto_sfx adds sounds for you instead: events title, transition and cta-tap, a seed, intensity subtle or normal, and title_sound pop, typing or sparkle; the job warnings list each sound added (variant, owner, time) and each event skipped with its reason. Sounds play alongside the clips, never change their speech volume or the video's length and are cut where the video ends. They are free and never leave your computer. Example: “Add a quiet interface click at 1.2 seconds and a bubble pop when the title 'My three tips' appears” is sfx [{asset:"ugc-click-01", start:1.2, gain:0.25}, {asset:"ugc-pop-01", anchor:{kind:"title-enter", text:0}}] with that title in texts. Caption lines: speech is cut into phrases of a few words; captions.grouping sets how, and captions.lines moves, sizes, rotates or restyles chosen phrases by v1 clip index and source seconds (a range covers whole phrases by their middle). captions.scatter gives every phrase its own position, size, small rotation and style from a styles list for one seed. Moving, sizing and rotating a phrase is free, and so are scatter styles and line styles from clean, boxed, minimal; any other line style (including mixed), a scatter styles list with one, or styled words needs Pro, so tell the user before rendering when a request uses them. clips[].captions_enabled false drops that v1 clip's speech from the captions; rapid_intro teasers show no captions unless captions_on_teasers is true. Build the whole edit in one call. Example: “Use these five clips in order, add a five-frame Rapid intro with these labels, generate captions with a different style and safe position for each short phrase using Scatter seed 58 with free styles, then export a vertical 720p MP4” is captions {style: "clean", position: "lower", size: "m", scatter: {seed: 58, safe_zone: "social", intensity: "normal", styles: ["clean", "boxed", "minimal"]}} with rapid_intro and quality 720p.

place.description: Destination box in the output. Custom coordinates are normalized, contained in the output. Omit for full.

rect.description: The part of the title box (its text plus padding) that is revealed, as fractions from its top left; width and height at least 0.01, inside the box. Omitted sides default to the whole box.

direction.description: The way the visible window grows: right starts at the left edge, left at the right edge, down at the top, up at the bottom. Default up.

start.description: Local seconds from the title's own start when the wipe begins; nothing of the title shows before it. Default 0.

easing.description: Shapes the wipe's progress: a named curve or a custom Bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2], each 0–1. Default ease-out.

reveal.description: A rectangular wipe that reveals the finished title over stationary text; omit the field for a plain title. Needs Pro to export (free to omit).

clip.description: Index in clips (v1 or v2, video or photo) whose people stand in front of the title. Required for a title placed with start and duration, which must overlap that clip in time; omit it, or give the title's own clip, for a title bound with clip.

threshold.description: How sure a pixel must be to count as a person. Default 0.5.

feather.description: Softness of the person's edge in mask pixels. Default 1.

smoothing.description: How much the two previous pictures steady the mask. Default 0.2.

occlusion.description: Put the title behind the people in one clip: it is drawn behind every detected person in that clip's picture, found on your computer with a small people model that ships inside the package. Needs Pro to export (free to omit).

clips.description: Indices of 5–7 distinct v1 clips in clips, in teaser order.

labels.description: Exactly one label for each chosen clip, supplied by the user or the assistant; the tool does not look at pictures.

frames_per_clip.description: Frames in each teaser cut. Default 5.

timestamp.description: Stamp above each body label: source (the clip's source in-point as mm:ss, default), timeline (its timeline start as mm:ss) or none. Photos cannot use source.

captions_on_teasers.description: Only in a request with captions. Default false: the teaser cuts show no captions, the body keeps them.

rapid_intro.description: Rapid intro: 5–7 v1 clips become teasers (the first frames of each clip's trim, no transitions) placed before the unchanged v1 body, whose clips get the labels. V2 starts, overlay starts and explicit titles move later by the teaser total.

start.description: Timeline seconds of the edit as you describe it before pause removal and any rapid intro, which move it with the edit. Give exactly one of start or anchor.

anchor.description: Follow an event instead of a fixed time. Exactly one of start or anchor.

text.description: Index in texts: the moment that title first appears.

after_clip.description: Request index of a v1 clip listed in transitions: the middle of a crossfade or the dip's black point.

cue.description: A tap id from that overlay's activeCues (configure_overlay).

offset.description: Seconds after (positive) or before the anchored event. Only with anchor; default 0.

in.description: Seconds into the sound where playback starts (not video time). Default the beginning.

out.description: Seconds into the sound where playback ends. Default the whole sound.

gain.description: Volume 0–2. Default is the sound's own quiet level.

mute.description: Keep the sound in the edit but silent. Default false.

items.description: One sound from the built-in pack.

events.description: title (a title appears), transition (a configured crossfade or dip; hard cuts and the rapid-intro teaser cuts get nothing) and cta-tap (a tap an overlay declares). Default all three.

seed.description: Picks between the two variants of a sound; the same seed gives the same choice. Default 58.

intensity.description: subtle plays the sounds quieter. Default normal.

title_sound.description: Kind of sound for titles. Default pop.

auto_sfx.description: Let the tool place sounds for you on the finished edit (after captions, pause removal and any rapid intro), with one sound per event, whooshes only at configured transitions and clicks only at taps the overlay declares. Events too close together keep the most important one. The job result lists what was added and what was skipped by owner, so tell the user which overlays have no tap.

style.description: mixed gives every word its own font, weight, color and spacing from three families.

mix.description: Only with style mixed. Presets: creator (Creator trio) and editorial (Editorial trio). The same seed and palette give the same look; omit seed for the default look.

grouping.description: How speech is cut into caption phrases (lines): a phrase ends at a pause of at least pause seconds, at max_words words, max_characters characters or max_duration seconds, or after a sentence. All four are required. Omit for the standard grouping (7 words, 32 characters, 30 seconds, 0.6 second pause); with scatter and no grouping it is 4 words, 24 characters, 1.8 seconds, 0.35 second pause.

scatter.description: Give every spoken phrase its own position, size, small rotation and style from styles, chosen by the seed (the same seed and speech give the same result) and kept clear of titles and overlays. social keeps text inside a conservative portrait feed area, frame inside the picture margin. subtle varies rotation and size less than normal. All four fields are required. Explicit lines rows win over it. Pro is needed only if styles holds an expressive style other than captions.style.

clip.description: Index of a v1 clip in clips.

mix.description: Only with style mixed. Presets: creator (Creator trio) and editorial (Editorial trio). The same seed and palette give the same look; omit seed for the default look.

items.description: from–to are source seconds of that v1 clip's own trim; the row applies to every whole phrase whose middle, (first word start + last word end) / 2, is in [from, to), so one range can change several phrases. x and y are the phrase block's centre as fractions of the output, size the font height as a fraction of the output's shorter side, rotation clockwise degrees. Needs at least one of x, y, size, rotation or style; mix goes with style mixed.

lines.description: Place or restyle chosen phrases by source seconds. Overlapping rows merge in request order. A row that reaches no spoken phrase, or whose phrases are gone after pause removal or the rapid intro, is an error naming it. At most 100 rows.

word_styles.description: Style spoken words by source seconds: every word whose midpoint falls in from–to of that v1 clip's own trim, after corrections. A range with no spoken words is an error. Needs Pro.

clip.description: Index of a v1 clip in clips.

appearance.description: At least one field. sans (Montserrat) weights 500/700/800/900; serif (Lora) 400/600/700 with italic; mono (Roboto Mono) 400/500/700. weight and italic need font. Tracking in em, leading as a line-height multiple, highlight false removes a highlight.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Transcribe English speech in one local video (up to 180 seconds) using an English speech model on your computer. Optional in/out trim seconds; returned line times are source seconds. The transcript text is returned to your assistant/provider, so call only when the user wants to review or correct it. Media and transcript are never sent to Modisign. First use downloads the speech model; later calls work offline. Use captions.corrections in edit_video to fix names/phrases.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Check a local video job's state and progress (0–1). A done job includes the local artifact path, MIME type, bytes, duration and any history warning. Jobs last for this server process.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running local video job and clean its temporary files. A completed artifact is retained.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Check whether Modisign is signed in and has current Pro access. Anonymous free overlays work without signing in. Returns sign-in instructions when needed.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Start Modisign device sign-in. Show the returned verification URL and code to the user; they sign in with Google and explicitly approve. Polling continues in the background. Use account_status to check completion. This tool never opens a browser or returns credentials.
